subject.title: Add confirmation step to /new and /reset to prevent accidental session wipes

question: Should manual `/new` and hard `/reset` require a default-on confirmation across all user-facing command surfaces, and should there be any config opt-out?
rationale: The source-level fix is bounded, but it changes public command semantics and may add a config/default surface, so automation should not choose the product contract on its own.

options.title: Default-On Single Confirmation
options.body: Require one repeated command or explicit confirm action before destructive manual resets, without adding a config knob unless maintainers approve a concrete opt-out need.

options.title: Configurable Confirmation
options.body: Add documented config for confirmation behavior and accept the extra schema, docs, migration, and upgrade-review burden.

options.title: Keep Commands Immediate
options.body: Leave typed `/new` and `/reset` unchanged and focus on non-destructive session creation or recovery improvements elsewhere.

recommendation.title: Default-On Single Confirmation
recommendation.body: Require one repeated command or explicit confirm action before destructive manual resets, without adding a config knob unless maintainers approve a concrete opt-out need.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc authored the existing partial confirmation guard and has the strongest history-backed ownership signal for deciding whether it becomes a cross-command contract.
